# AnvilUI documentation (all pages)

Generated from core/AGENTS.md and core/docs/*.md. Relative links point into the docs/ folder.

<!-- file: AGENTS.md -->

# AnvilUI: reference for AI coding agents

`anvilui` is a React 19 component library with Material 3 styling, built on [Base UI](https://base-ui.com) (`@base-ui/react`). It has ~50 accessible components (buttons, inputs, selects, dialogs, menus, navigation, …), a theme system driven by CSS variables, and Material Symbols icons referenced by name. It is **not** shadcn/ui, Radix or MUI: names and props differ. This file matches the installed version. Read it before writing code; per-component pages are in [`docs/`](docs/llms-index.md) (`node_modules/anvilui/docs/<name>.md`).

## Rules that prevent most errors

1. `import 'anvilui/styles.css'` once, and wrap the whole app in `<AnvilRoot>`. Nothing is themed outside it.
2. Everything imports from `'anvilui'`. No subpaths (`anvilui/button` doesn't exist) except `'anvilui/styles.css'`.
3. **No `asChild`.** Use `render`: `<DialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Open</DialogTrigger>`. Trigger and Close parts render bare, unstyled buttons without it.
4. **No `variant`.** Style is `fillType: 'filled' | 'outlined' | 'text'`; color is `color: 'primary' | 'tonal' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'container' | 'surface'`. No `secondary` / `destructive` / `ghost`.
5. **Icons are strings** (Material Symbols names): `startIcon="add"`, `<IconButton icon="delete" aria-label="Delete" />`, `<Icon name="home" />`. Don't pass icon components.
6. Callbacks get **values, not events**: `onValueChange(value)`, `onCheckedChange(checked)`, `onOpenChange(open)`, `onPressedChange(pressed)`. No `onChange` except on `Input`/`Textarea` (native).
7. `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `Radio` have **no `label` prop**: wrap them in `<label>`. Most other controls take `label`.
8. Titles and text often go in **`label`, not children**: `AppBar`, `ListItem`, `Tooltip`, nav items, `Input`, `Select`, `Slider`, `Progress`.
9. Icon-only controls require `aria-label` (`IconButton`, `FAB` without `label`, icon `Toggle`, `Slider`/`Progress` without `label`, `Search`, `Carousel`).
10. `Button` defaults to `type="button"`. Use `type="submit"` in forms.
11. Dates are `"YYYY-MM-DD"` strings, times `"HH:mm"` strings. Not `Date` objects.
12. No layout components (`Box`, `Stack`, `Grid`, `Container`, `Flex`) and no `sx`. Use plain elements with `style` / CSS and theme variables like `var(--avl-spacing-x4)`.

## Setup

Requires `react` and `react-dom` 19+, and a bundler that handles CSS from `node_modules` (Vite, Next.js, webpack).

```tsx
// main.tsx
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'
import { AnvilRoot } from 'anvilui'
import 'anvilui/styles.css'
import { App } from './App'

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
    <AnvilRoot
        defaultColorMode="system"
        storageKey="color-mode"
        className="app-root"
    >
        <App />
    </AnvilRoot>
)
```

- `AnvilRoot` is the only provider (theme, color mode, tooltips, snackbars, portal container). Don't add `ThemeProvider`, `Toaster` or `TooltipProvider`.
- Give it a class with `min-height: 100vh` so the background covers the page.
- Hooks `useAnvil()` and `useSnackbar()` work only in components **inside** it.
- Next.js App Router: render `AnvilRoot` in a `'use client'` component and use AnvilUI from client components. Details: [docs/setup.md](docs/setup.md).
- Fonts: Google Sans is not loaded for you (falls back to the system font). See setup.md.

Nothing else is exported. Not in the library: `Box`, `Stack`, `Grid`, `Container`, `Label`, `FieldLabel`, `Form`, `Spinner`, `Toast`/`Toaster`, `Alert`, `Banner`, `Breadcrumbs`, `Pagination`, `Stepper`, `DataGrid`, `DatePicker` (use `DateInput`), `Drawer` (use `NavigationDrawer` / `BottomSheet`), `DropdownMenu` (use `Menu`), `Separator` (use `Divider`), `Sheet` (use `BottomSheet`).

## Component reference

Props marked * are required. All components also take `className`, `style`, `ref` and the props of their underlying element / Base UI part. Full tables: `docs/<name>.md`.

### Buttons

| Component | Key props | Usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Button` | `fillType`, `color`, `size: 'small'\|'normal'\|'big'`, `startIcon`, `endIcon`, `loading`, `disabled`, `type`, `render` | `<Button startIcon="add" onClick={create}>New</Button>` |
| `IconButton` | `icon`_, `aria-label`_, `fillType`, `color`. No size, no children | `<IconButton icon="close" aria-label="Close" fillType="text" color="container" />` |
| `SplitButton` | `<div>` props | `<SplitButton><Button>Save</Button><IconButton icon="arrow_drop_down" aria-label="More" /></SplitButton>` |
| `HoldButton` | `onConfirm`*, `holdDuration` (1500), Button props | `<HoldButton color="error" onConfirm={del}>Hold to delete</HoldButton>` |
| `Toggle` | `pressed`/`defaultPressed`/`onPressedChange`, `color`, `fillType`; text: `children`, `startIcon`, `size`; icon: `icon` + `aria-label` | `<Toggle icon="favorite" aria-label="Favorite" />` |
| `ToggleGroup` | `value`/`defaultValue`/`onValueChange` (single value; array with `multiple`), `multiple`, `color`, `fillType`, `size` | `<ToggleGroup aria-label="View" defaultValue="list">…</ToggleGroup>` |
| `ToggleGroupItem` | `value`*, `startIcon`, `endIcon`, `children` | `<ToggleGroupItem value="list">List</ToggleGroupItem>` |
| `FAB` | `icon`_, `label` or `aria-label`_, `size`, `color`, `fillType`, `sticky` | `<FAB icon="add" aria-label="New" style={{ position: 'fixed', right: 16, bottom: 16 }} />` |
| `FABMenu` | `icon`_, `aria-label`_, `children`* (`FABMenuItem`s), `side`, `align`, `color` | `<FABMenu icon="add" aria-label="Create"><FABMenuItem icon="folder">Folder</FABMenuItem></FABMenu>` |
| `Chip` / `FilterChip` / `InputChip` | `startIcon`; FilterChip `pressed`/`onPressedChange`; InputChip `onRemove`*, `removeLabel` | `<FilterChip pressed={on} onPressedChange={setOn}>Vegan</FilterChip>` |

### Form controls

| Component | Key props | Usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | `label`, `size: 'small'\|'normal'`, `value`/`defaultValue`, `onValueChange(string)` or `onChange(event)`, input attrs | `<Input label="Email" type="email" value={v} onValueChange={setV} />` |
| `Textarea` | same as Input + `rows` | `<Textarea label="Bio" rows={4} />` |
| `Select` | `items` (map or `{value,label}[]`), `value`/`defaultValue`/`onValueChange(value)`, `label`, `placeholder`, `multiple`, `name` | `<Select label="Fruit" items={fruits} defaultValue="apple">{…SelectItem}</Select>` |
| `SelectItem` | `value`*, children = label | `<SelectItem value="apple">Apple</SelectItem>` |
| `Combobox` | `items`, `children`* = `(item) => <ComboboxItem/>`, `value`/`onValueChange(item)`, `itemToStringLabel`, `label`, `empty` | `<Combobox label="Fruit" items={list}>{(f: string) => <ComboboxItem key={f} value={f}>{f}</ComboboxItem>}</Combobox>` |
| `Search` | `aria-label`_, `items`, `children`_ = `(item) => <SearchItem/>`, `value`/`onValueChange(text)`, `placeholder`, `empty` | `<Search aria-label="Search" items={[]} onValueChange={setQ}>{(i: string) => <SearchItem key={i} value={i}>{i}</SearchItem>}</Search>` |
| `Checkbox` | `checked`/`defaultChecked`/`onCheckedChange(boolean)`, `indeterminate`, `name` | `<label><Checkbox checked={c} onCheckedChange={setC} /> Remember me</label>` |
| `Switch` | `checked`/`defaultChecked`/`onCheckedChange(boolean)`, `name` | `<label><Switch defaultChecked /> Wi-Fi</label>` |
| `RadioGroup` / `Radio` | group: `value`/`defaultValue`/`onValueChange(value)`, `name`; radio: `value`* | `<RadioGroup defaultValue="a"><label><Radio value="a" /> A</label></RadioGroup>` |
| `Slider` | `label` or `aria-label`*, `value`/`defaultValue` (number or number[]), `onValueChange(number)`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `showValue`, `format` | `<Slider label="Volume" defaultValue={50} />` |
| `DateInput` | `value`/`defaultValue` `"YYYY-MM-DD" \| null`, `onValueChange`, `label` or `aria-label`* | `<DateInput label="Due" value={d} onValueChange={setD} />` |
| `TimePicker` | `value`/`defaultValue` `"HH:mm" \| null`, `onValueChange`, `type: 'dial'\|'input'`, `hourCycle: 12\|24`, `label` or `aria-label`*, `name` | `<TimePicker label="Start" defaultValue="09:00" />` |
| `Calendar` | `value`/`defaultValue` `"YYYY-MM-DD" \| null`, `onValueChange` | `<Calendar value={d} onValueChange={setD} />` |
| `PinInput` | `length`_, `label` or `aria-label`_, `value`/`onValueChange`, `onValueComplete`, `mask`, `validationType` | `<PinInput label="Code" length={6} />` |
| `Field` | `name`, `validate`, `validationMode: 'onSubmit'\|'onBlur'\|'onChange'`, `invalid`, `disabled` | `<Field name="email"><Input label="Email" required /><FieldError /></Field>` |
| `FieldDescription` / `FieldError` | FieldError `match` | `<FieldError match="valueMissing">Required</FieldError>` |

### Overlays and menus

| Component | Parts and key props | Usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | `open`/`defaultOpen`/`onOpenChange`; `DialogTrigger`, `DialogPopup` (includes portal + backdrop), `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogActions`, `DialogClose` | see Patterns |
| `BottomSheet` | same shape: `BottomSheetTrigger`, `BottomSheetPopup`, `BottomSheetTitle`, `BottomSheetDescription`, `BottomSheetClose`; `snapPoints` | |
| `Popover` | `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverPopup` (`side`, `align`, `sideOffset`), `PopoverTitle`, `PopoverDescription`, `PopoverClose` | |
| `PreviewCard` | `PreviewCardTrigger` (an `<a href>`), `PreviewCardPopup` | |
| `Tooltip` | `label`_, one element child_, `side`, `align`, `delay` | `<Tooltip label="Delete"><IconButton icon="delete" aria-label="Delete" /></Tooltip>` |
| `Menu` | `MenuTrigger`, `MenuPopup` (`side`, `align`), `MenuItem` (`onClick`, `startIcon`, `endIcon`, `disabled`), `MenuGroup`, `MenuSubmenu` + `MenuSubmenuTrigger` | see Patterns |
| `ContextMenu` | `ContextMenuTrigger` (area) + `MenuPopup` / `MenuItem` | |
| `Menubar` | contains `Menu`s | |
| `useSnackbar()` | `.show({ message*, action?: { label, onClick }, closeButton, timeout (5000), priority })`, `.close(id?)` | `snackbar.show({ message: 'Saved' })` |

### Navigation and layout

| Component | Key props | Usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AppBar` | `label`*, `labelAs`, `start`, `end`, `size: 'normal'\|'big'`, `centered`, `color` ('container') | `<AppBar label="Inbox" start={…} end={…} />` |
| `NavigationBar` / `NavigationBarItem` | item: `icon`_, `label`_, `active`, `href` or `render={<Link/>}` | `<NavigationBarItem icon="home" label="Home" href="/" active />` |
| `NavigationRail` / `NavigationRailToggle` / `NavigationRailItem` | rail: `expanded`/`defaultExpanded`/`onExpandedChange`; toggle: `aria-label`_; item: `icon`_, `label`*, `active`, `end`, `href` | |
| `NavigationList` / `NavigationListItem` | item: `label`*, `active`, `href`, `render` | |
| `NavigationDrawer` | `NavigationDrawerTrigger`, `NavigationDrawerPopup`, `NavigationDrawerTitle`, `NavigationDrawerItem` (`icon`_, `label`_, `active`, `href`) | |
| `Tabs` | `value`/`defaultValue`/`onValueChange`; `TabsList`, `TabsTab` (`value`_, `icon`), `TabsPanel` (`value`_). Always set `defaultValue` | see Patterns |
| `FloatingToolbar` | `inverseColor`; `FloatingToolbarButton` (IconButton props), `FloatingToolbarSeparator` | |
| `Card` | `color` ('container'), `fillType`, `clickable`; `CardTitle` (`as`), `CardContent`, `CardActions` | |
| `List` / `ListItem` | list: `divided`; item: `label`*, `description`, `start`, `end`, `render`. No children | `<ListItem label="Wi-Fi" end={<Switch />} render={<label />} />` |
| `Table` | `TableCaption`, `TableHead`, `TableBody`, `TableRow`, `TableHeaderCell`, `TableCell` (native elements) | |
| `Accordion` | `value`/`defaultValue` (array), `multiple`; `AccordionItem` (`value`), `AccordionTrigger` (`as`), `AccordionPanel` | |
| `Carousel` / `CarouselItem` | `aria-label`* | |
| `Divider` | `orientation`, `label`, `squiggly` | `<Divider label="or" />` |
| `Typography` | `type: 'body'\|'caption'\|'h1'…'h6'` (not `variant`), `as` | `<Typography type="h5" as="h1">Settings</Typography>` |

### Display

| Component | Key props | Usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Avatar` | `name`, `src`, `icon`, `size` (32/40/56px), `color` | `<Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" src={url} />` |
| `AvatarGroup` | `max`, `size`, `fan`, `aria-label` | `<AvatarGroup max={3} aria-label="Team">{avatars}</AvatarGroup>` |
| `Badge` | `count` (omit for dot, 0 hides), `max`, `color` ('error'), wraps children | `<Badge count={3}><IconButton icon="mail" aria-label="Mail, 3 new" /></Badge>` |
| `Icon` | `name`* | `<Icon name="star" />` |
| `Progress` | `value`* (`number \| null`), `type: 'linear'\|'circular'\|'inline'`, `label` or `aria-label`*, `squiggly` | `<Progress type="circular" value={null} aria-label="Loading" />` |
| `Skeleton` | `variant: 'text'\|'circular'\|'rectangular'`, `animation`; size via `style` | `<Skeleton style={{ width: 120 }} />` |
| `Sticker` | `color`, `startIcon`, `tilt` | `<Sticker>NEW</Sticker>` |
| `AnimatedNumber` | `value`*, `format`, `locales` | `<AnimatedNumber value={n} />` |
| `Kbd` | `children`, `listen`, `listenFor` | `<Kbd>⌘</Kbd><Kbd>K</Kbd>` |

## Patterns

### App shell: app bar, side navigation, content

```tsx
import {
    AppBar,
    Avatar,
    IconButton,
    NavigationRail,
    NavigationRailItem,
    NavigationRailToggle,
} from 'anvilui'

export function Shell({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', height: '100vh' }}>
            <NavigationRail aria-label="Main">
                <NavigationRailToggle aria-label="Toggle navigation" />
                <NavigationRailItem
                    icon="dashboard"
                    label="Dashboard"
                    href="/"
                    active
                />
                <NavigationRailItem
                    icon="settings"
                    label="Settings"
                    href="/settings"
                />
            </NavigationRail>
            <div
                style={{
                    flex: 1,
                    display: 'flex',
                    flexDirection: 'column',
                    minWidth: 0,
                }}
            >
                <AppBar
                    label="Dashboard"
                    labelAs="h1"
                    end={
                        <>
                            <IconButton
                                icon="notifications"
                                aria-label="Notifications"
                                fillType="text"
                                color="container"
                            />
                            <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" size="small" />
                        </>
                    }
                />
                <main
                    style={{
                        flex: 1,
                        overflow: 'auto',
                        padding: 'var(--avl-spacing-x6)',
                    }}
                >
                    {children}
                </main>
            </div>
        </div>
    )
}
```

### Settings page: tabs, form fields, switches

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import {
    Button,
    Field,
    FieldError,
    Input,
    List,
    ListItem,
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    Switch,
    Tabs,
    TabsList,
    TabsPanel,
    TabsTab,
    useSnackbar,
} from 'anvilui'

const languages = { en: 'English', fr: 'Français', ja: '日本語' }

export function Settings() {
    const snackbar = useSnackbar()
    const [name, setName] = useState('Ada')
    const [language, setLanguage] = useState<string | null>('en')
    return (
        <Tabs defaultValue="profile">
            <TabsList>
                <TabsTab value="profile" icon="person">
                    Profile
                </TabsTab>
                <TabsTab value="notifications" icon="notifications">
                    Notifications
                </TabsTab>
            </TabsList>
            <TabsPanel value="profile">
                <form
                    style={{
                        display: 'grid',
                        gap: 16,
                        maxWidth: 400,
                        paddingBlock: 16,
                    }}
                    onSubmit={(e) => {
                        e.preventDefault()
                        snackbar.show({ message: 'Profile saved' })
                    }}
                >
                    <Field name="name">
                        <Input
                            label="Display name"
                            required
                            value={name}
                            onValueChange={setName}
                        />
                        <FieldError />
                    </Field>
                    <Select
                        label="Language"
                        items={languages}
                        value={language}
                        onValueChange={setLanguage}
                    >
                        {Object.entries(languages).map(([value, label]) => (
                            <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>
                                {label}
                            </SelectItem>
                        ))}
                    </Select>
                    <Button type="submit" style={{ justifySelf: 'start' }}>
                        Save
                    </Button>
                </form>
            </TabsPanel>
            <TabsPanel value="notifications">
                <List divided>
                    <ListItem
                        label="Email"
                        description="Weekly summary"
                        end={<Switch defaultChecked />}
                        render={<label />}
                    />
                    <ListItem
                        label="Push"
                        end={<Switch />}
                        render={<label />}
                    />
                </List>
            </TabsPanel>
        </Tabs>
    )
}
```

### Confirm dialog opened from a row menu

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import {
    Button,
    Dialog,
    DialogActions,
    DialogClose,
    DialogDescription,
    DialogPopup,
    DialogTitle,
    IconButton,
    List,
    ListItem,
    Menu,
    MenuItem,
    MenuPopup,
    MenuTrigger,
} from 'anvilui'

export function Files() {
    const [files, setFiles] = useState(['report.pdf', 'notes.txt'])
    // Separate from `open`, so the title still reads right while it animates closed
    const [toDelete, setToDelete] = useState('')
    const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
    return (
        <>
            <List divided>
                {files.map((file) => (
                    <ListItem
                        key={file}
                        label={file}
                        end={
                            <Menu>
                                <MenuTrigger
                                    render={
                                        <IconButton
                                            icon="more_vert"
                                            aria-label={`Actions for ${file}`}
                                            fillType="text"
                                            color="container"
                                        />
                                    }
                                />
                                <MenuPopup align="end">
                                    <MenuItem
                                        startIcon="delete"
                                        onClick={() => {
                                            setToDelete(file)
                                            setOpen(true)
                                        }}
                                    >
                                        Delete
                                    </MenuItem>
                                </MenuPopup>
                            </Menu>
                        }
                    />
                ))}
            </List>
            {/* Controlled, outside the menu, so closing the menu doesn't unmount it */}
            <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
                <DialogPopup>
                    <DialogTitle>Delete {toDelete}?</DialogTitle>
                    <DialogDescription>This can't be undone.</DialogDescription>
                    <DialogActions>
                        <DialogClose render={<Button fillType="text" />}>
                            Cancel
                        </DialogClose>
                        <Button
                            color="error"
                            onClick={() => {
                                setFiles(files.filter((f) => f !== toDelete))
                                setOpen(false)
                            }}
                        >
                            Delete
                        </Button>
                    </DialogActions>
                </DialogPopup>
            </Dialog>
        </>
    )
}
```

### Router links

Nav items, `ListItem`, `MenuItem`, `PreviewCardTrigger` and `Card clickable` take `render`: `<NavigationRailItem icon="home" label="Home" render={<Link to="/" />} active={pathname === '/'} />`. On `Button` also pass `nativeButton={false}`: `<Button render={<Link to="/new" />} nativeButton={false}>New</Button>`.

### Switching views without URLs

Nav items render `<a>` by default. For in-page state, pass a plain button: `<NavigationRailItem icon="home" label="Home" active={view === 'home'} render={<button type="button" onClick={() => setView('home')} />} />` (no `nativeButton` needed). Same for `NavigationBarItem`, `NavigationListItem`, `NavigationDrawerItem` (still closes the drawer) and `ListItem`.

### Inline success / error messages

There is no `Alert` or `Banner`. For a message after an action, use a snackbar (`useSnackbar().show(...)`). For a message that stays on the page, use a colored card: `<Card color="success" role="status"><CardContent>Account created</CardContent></Card>` (`color="error"` with `role="alert"` for errors). For a field's error, use `Field` + `FieldError`.

### Typing state for value callbacks

`Value` is inferred from your `value` / `defaultValue`, so union-typed state works directly: `const [plan, setPlan] = useState<'free' | 'pro'>('free')` then `<ToggleGroup value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>` (also `RadioGroup`, `Tabs`, `Select`). `Slider` too: a number `value` gives a `(value: number)` callback, an array a `number[]` one, so `onValueChange={setVolume}` works. To type an icon field yourself: `import type { MaterialSymbol } from 'anvilui'`.

### Theme colors in your own CSS

Inside AnvilRoot: `var(--avl-color-background)`, `var(--avl-color-on-background)`, `var(--avl-color-on-background-muted)`, `var(--avl-color-primary)`, `var(--avl-color-surface)`, `var(--avl-color-divider)`, spacing `var(--avl-spacing-x1…x20)` (4px steps), radius `var(--avl-radius-medium)`. Custom brand: `createTheme('#0B6E4F')` → `<AnvilRoot lightTheme={t.light} darkTheme={t.dark}>` ([theming.md](docs/theming.md)).

## Common mistakes

| Wrong (other libraries) | Right (AnvilUI) |
| --- | --- |
| `<Button variant="outline">` | `<Button fillType="outlined">` |
| `<Button variant="ghost">` / `variant="link"` | `<Button fillType="text">` |
| `<Button variant="destructive">` / `color="danger"` | `<Button color="error">` |
| `<Button variant="secondary">` / `color="secondary"` | `<Button color="container">` or `color="tonal"` |
| `<Button size="lg">` / `size="sm"` | `size="big"` / `size="small"` |
| `<Button><Plus /> Add</Button>` | `<Button startIcon="add">Add</Button>` |
| `<IconButton><DeleteIcon /></IconButton>` | `<IconButton icon="delete" aria-label="Delete" />` |
| `<IconButton icon="x" size="small" />` | IconButton has no `size`; it's always 40px |
| `<DialogTrigger asChild><Button>Open</Button></DialogTrigger>` | `<DialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Open</DialogTrigger>` |
| `<DialogTrigger>Open</DialogTrigger>` expecting a styled button | It's a bare `<button>`; add `render={<Button />}` |
| `<DialogContent>`, `<DialogHeader>`, `<DialogFooter>` | `<DialogPopup>`, (nothing), `<DialogActions>` |
| `<Dialog><DialogPortal><DialogOverlay/>…` | `DialogPopup` already includes portal and backdrop |
| `<Tooltip content="Hi">` / `<TooltipTrigger>` | `<Tooltip label="Hi"><IconButton … /></Tooltip>` |
| `<Tooltip label="Hi">text</Tooltip>` | One element child: `<Tooltip label="Hi"><span tabIndex={0}>text</span></Tooltip>` |
| `<Checkbox label="Accept" />` | `<label><Checkbox /> Accept</label>` |
| `<Switch onChange={(e) => set(e.target.checked)} />` | `<Switch onCheckedChange={set} />` |
| `<Select onChange={(e) => set(e.target.value)}>` | `<Select onValueChange={set}>` |
| `<Select><SelectTrigger/><SelectContent>…` | `<Select label="…" items={items}><SelectItem value="a">A</SelectItem></Select>` |
| `<Select>` without `items` showing `"us"` instead of "United States" | pass `items={{ us: 'United States' }}` (or `[{ value, label }]`) |
| `<Combobox><ComboboxItem/>…</Combobox>` | `<Combobox items={list}>{(item) => <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>}</Combobox>` |
| `<Tabs><TabsTrigger/><TabsContent/>` | `<Tabs defaultValue="a"><TabsList><TabsTab value="a">A</TabsTab></TabsList><TabsPanel value="a">…</TabsPanel></Tabs>` |
| `<Tabs>` with string values and no `defaultValue` (nothing selected) | always pass `defaultValue` / `value` |
| `<Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="a">` | `<Accordion defaultValue={['a']}>` (array; `multiple` for several) |
| `<DropdownMenu>`, `<DropdownMenuItem onSelect>` | `<Menu>`, `<MenuItem onClick>` |
| `<MenuSeparator />` | split items into `<MenuGroup>`s |
| `toast('Saved')`, `<Toaster />`, `<Snackbar open>` | `const snackbar = useSnackbar(); snackbar.show({ message: 'Saved' })` |
| `snackbar.show({ message, severity: 'success' })` | no severity; put it in the message |
| `<Typography variant="h4">` | `<Typography type="h4">` |
| `<AppBar title="Inbox">` / `<AppBar>Inbox</AppBar>` | `<AppBar label="Inbox" />` |
| `<ListItem>Text</ListItem>` / `primary=` / `secondary=` | `<ListItem label="Text" description="More" />` |
| `<ListItem onClick={…} />` expecting a button | `<ListItem label="…" render={<button type="button" onClick={…} />} />` |
| `<CardHeader>`, `<CardFooter>`, `<CardDescription>` | `<CardTitle>`, `<CardActions>`, `<CardContent>` |
| `<Badge badgeContent={3}>` | `<Badge count={3}>` |
| `<Progress value={undefined} />` for loading / `<Spinner />` | `<Progress value={null} aria-label="Loading" />` (`type="circular"` for a ring) |
| `<DateInput value={new Date()} />` | `value="2026-11-06"` (`"YYYY-MM-DD"` string) |
| `<TimePicker value="7:30 PM" />` | `value="19:30"` |
| `<Slider onValueChange={(e) => …e.target.value} />` | `onValueChange={(value) => …}` gets the number |
| `<Input error helperText="…" />` | `<Field><Input … /><FieldDescription>…</FieldDescription><FieldError /></Field>` |
| `<Button>` inside `<form>` not submitting | `<Button type="submit">` (default is `type="button"`) |
| `<ThemeProvider theme={…}>` | `<AnvilRoot lightTheme={…} darkTheme={…}>` |
| `useSnackbar()` / `useAnvil()` in the component that renders `<AnvilRoot>` | call them in a child component |
| `import { Button } from 'anvilui/button'` | `import { Button } from 'anvilui'` |
| Forgetting `import 'anvilui/styles.css'` | import it once in the entry file |
| `<Stack gap={2}>`, `<Box sx={…}>` | `<div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--avl-spacing-x2)' }}>` |

## Errors you may see

In development, AnvilUI logs `[anvilui] …` errors with a fix and a doc path for: a missing stylesheet, components outside `AnvilRoot`, `asChild`, `variant` on Button/IconButton/Typography, `label` on Checkbox/Switch/Radio, missing `aria-label`, non-function Combobox/Search children, a Tooltip without one element child, and parts outside their parent. Base UI's own errors look like `Base UI: MenuRootContext is missing. Menu parts must be placed within <Menu.Root>`. `<Menu.Root>` there means AnvilUI's `<Menu>` (likewise `<Tabs.Root>` → `<Tabs>`, `<Dialog.Root>` → `<Dialog>`).

## More

- Routing index of all pages: [docs/llms-index.md](docs/llms-index.md)
- Inherited Base UI props for any part: `node_modules/@base-ui/react/docs/react/components/<name>.md`
- Types with JSDoc on every prop: `node_modules/anvilui/dist/index.d.ts`

---

<!-- file: docs/setup.md -->

# Setup

Install, import the stylesheet, wrap the app in `AnvilRoot`. All three are required.

## Install

```sh
npm install anvilui
```

| Requirement | Version | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `react`, `react-dom` | **19 or newer** | Uses React 19 features (`ref` as a prop, `<Context value>`). React 18 does not work. |
| A bundler that handles CSS imports from `node_modules` | Vite, Next.js, webpack, Parcel | `anvilui` imports `material-symbols/rounded.css` (the icon font). |
| `@base-ui/react`, `material-symbols` | installed automatically | Regular dependencies; don't install them yourself. |

## 1. Import the stylesheet once

```ts
// main.tsx, app/layout.tsx, or your entry file
import 'anvilui/styles.css'
```

Without it every component renders unstyled. In development, AnvilRoot logs `[anvilui] The AnvilUI stylesheet isn't loaded` when it's missing.

## 2. Wrap the app in `AnvilRoot`

```tsx
import { AnvilRoot, Button } from 'anvilui'
import 'anvilui/styles.css'

export function App() {
    return (
        <AnvilRoot defaultColorMode="system" className="app">
            <Button>Hello</Button>
        </AnvilRoot>
    )
}
```

`AnvilRoot` is the only provider. It:

- defines the theme as CSS variables on its own `<div class="avl-root">`. Styles only apply inside it.
- is the container that menus, dialogs, popovers, selects and tooltips portal into. Outside it they render unthemed.
- provides `useSnackbar()` (it renders the snackbar viewport) and shares tooltip delays.
- holds the color mode (`useAnvil()`).

Put it once at the top, around everything (inside `<StrictMode>` is fine). Don't nest it per page, and don't call `useAnvil()` / `useSnackbar()` in the same component that renders it.

To theme the whole page, make the root fill the viewport:

```css
.app {
    min-height: 100vh;
}
```

## 3. Fonts (optional)

The default theme uses Google Sans and Google Sans Code and falls back to the system font. AnvilUI does not load fonts. To get them, add to `<head>`:

```html
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
<link
    rel="stylesheet"
    href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Google+Sans+Code:ital,wght,MONO@0,300..800,1;1,300..800,1&family=Google+Sans:ital,opsz,wght@0,17..18,400..700;1,17..18,400..700&display=swap"
/>
```

Other fonts: pass `tokens={{ font: { main: '...', title: '...', mono: '...' } }}` to AnvilRoot (see [theming.md](theming.md)).

## Next.js (App Router)

`AnvilRoot` uses state and effects, so render it from a client component:

```tsx
'use client'
import { AnvilRoot } from 'anvilui'
import 'anvilui/styles.css'

export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
    return <AnvilRoot storageKey="color-mode">{children}</AnvilRoot>
}
```

Then use `<Providers>` in `app/layout.tsx` inside `<body>`. Every AnvilUI component is interactive; use them from client components (`'use client'`). With `storageKey`, the saved color mode is applied before the first paint, with no flash.

## Without a bundler

Not supported. The package imports CSS and relies on the bundler to replace `process.env.NODE_ENV`.

## Styling your own elements

Inside AnvilRoot, theme values are CSS variables you can use in your own CSS:

| Need | Variable |
| --- | --- |
| page background / text | `var(--avl-color-background)`, `var(--avl-color-on-background)` |
| secondary text | `var(--avl-color-on-background-muted)` |
| any theme color | `var(--avl-color-<role>)`, e.g. `--avl-color-primary`, `--avl-color-on-primary`, `--avl-color-surface` |
| spacing | `var(--avl-spacing-x1)` … `var(--avl-spacing-x20)` (4px steps by default) |
| radius | `var(--avl-radius-small \| medium \| large \| full)` |
| font size | `var(--avl-font-size-body \| caption \| label \| h1 … h6)` |

There is no `Box`, `Stack`, `Grid` or `Container` component, and no `sx` prop. Use plain elements with `style` or your own CSS for layout.

---

<!-- file: docs/theming.md -->

# Theming and color mode

Colors come from a `Theme` (light and dark), everything else from `DesignTokens`. Both are props on `AnvilRoot`.

```ts
import {
    AnvilRoot,
    useAnvil,
    createTheme,
    createThemeFromImage,
    baseLightTheme,
    baseDarkTheme,
    monochromeLightTheme,
    monochromeDarkTheme,
    baseDesignTokens,
} from 'anvilui'
import type {
    Theme,
    ThemePair,
    DesignTokens,
    ColorModeSetting,
    ColorType,
} from 'anvilui'
```

## AnvilRoot props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | required | The app. |
| `className` | `string` | | Classes for the root `<div>`, e.g. to fill the viewport. |
| `colorMode` | `'light' \| 'dark' \| 'system'` | | Controlled color mode. Pair with `onColorModeChange`. |
| `defaultColorMode` | `'light' \| 'dark' \| 'system'` | `'system'` | Starting mode when uncontrolled. `'system'` follows the OS live. |
| `onColorModeChange` | `(mode: ColorModeSetting) => void` | | Called when the mode changes. |
| `storageKey` | `string` | | Saves the mode in `localStorage` under this key and restores it (no flash with SSR). |
| `lightTheme` | `Theme` | `baseLightTheme` | Colors in light mode. |
| `darkTheme` | `Theme` | `baseDarkTheme` | Colors in dark mode. |
| `tokens` | `Partial<DesignTokens>` | `baseDesignTokens` | Spacing, radius, fonts, motion, shadows. Each category you pass **replaces** the whole default category. |

AnvilRoot renders a `<div>` and takes no other props (no `style`, `id`, `theme`).

## Color mode

```tsx
import { AnvilRoot, IconButton, useAnvil } from 'anvilui'

function ModeToggle() {
    const { colorMode, setColorMode } = useAnvil()
    return (
        <IconButton
            icon={colorMode === 'dark' ? 'light_mode' : 'dark_mode'}
            aria-label="Toggle dark mode"
            fillType="text"
            color="container"
            onClick={() =>
                setColorMode(colorMode === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark')
            }
        />
    )
}

export function App() {
    return (
        <AnvilRoot storageKey="color-mode">
            <ModeToggle />
        </AnvilRoot>
    )
}
```

`useAnvil()` returns:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `colorMode` | `'light' \| 'dark'` | What's shown now (`'system'` resolved). |
| `colorModeSetting` | `'light' \| 'dark' \| 'system'` | What was picked. |
| `setColorMode` | `Dispatch<SetStateAction<ColorModeSetting>>` | Like a `useState` setter. |
| `lightTheme`, `darkTheme` | `Theme` | The themes in use. |
| `tokens` | `DesignTokens` | The tokens in use, defaults filled in. |
| `rootRef` | `RefObject<HTMLDivElement \| null>` | The root element (the portal container). |

`useAnvil()` throws outside `AnvilRoot`.

## Custom colors

```tsx
import { AnvilRoot, Button, createTheme } from 'anvilui'

// Module scope (or useMemo): it does color math
const brand = createTheme('#0B6E4F', { tonal: '#6E4F0B' })

export function App() {
    return (
        <AnvilRoot lightTheme={brand.light} darkTheme={brand.dark}>
            <Button>Brand colored</Button>
        </AnvilRoot>
    )
}
```

- `createTheme(primaryHex, { tonal?: hex })` returns `{ light: Theme, dark: Theme }`. Hex only (`'#0B6E4F'` or `'#0B6'`); other formats throw.
- `createThemeFromImage(img | File | Blob | url)` returns `Promise<ThemePair>`, browser only. URLs must allow CORS.
- Error, warning and success colors stay the same.
- Tweak one role by spreading: `{ ...brand.light, primary: '#…' }`.
- Ready-made: `baseLightTheme` / `baseDarkTheme` (purple, the default), `monochromeLightTheme` / `monochromeDarkTheme`.

## Theme roles

`Theme` is an object of color strings. Each `x` has an `onX` for text on it.

| Role | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `background` / `onBackground` / `onBackgroundMuted` | Page and body text; muted is secondary text |
| `container` / `onContainer` | Neutral fills: cards, chips, inputs, "secondary" buttons |
| `surface` / `onSurface` | Navigation, menus, dialogs, sheets |
| `primary` / `onPrimary`, `primaryContainer` / `onPrimaryContainer` | Brand color |
| `tonal` / `onTonal`, `tonalContainer` / `onTonalContainer` | Softer accent: selected states, tonal buttons |
| `error`, `warning`, `success` (+ `on…`, `…Container`, `on…Container`) | Status colors |
| `outline` | Borders of inputs and outlined controls |
| `divider` | Lines between content |
| `inverseSurface`, `inverseOnSurface`, `inversePrimary` (optional) | Tooltips, snackbars |
| `shadow`, `scrim` (optional) | Shadow color, dialog backdrop |

Each role is a CSS variable in kebab case: `primaryContainer` → `var(--avl-color-primary-container)`.

## Component colors (`color` prop)

Components take `color` from these roles only:

```ts
type ComponentColor =
    | 'primary'
    | 'tonal'
    | 'success'
    | 'warning'
    | 'error'
    | 'container'
    | 'surface'
type ComponentFillType = 'filled' | 'outlined' | 'text'
```

There is no `secondary`, `danger`, `destructive`, `info` or `default`. Use `tonal` or `container` for secondary actions and `error` for destructive ones.

## Tokens

```tsx
import { AnvilRoot, baseDesignTokens } from 'anvilui'

export function App() {
    return (
        <AnvilRoot
            tokens={{
                // A category replaces the whole default one, so spread it
                radius: {
                    ...baseDesignTokens.radius,
                    medium: '8px',
                    large: '12px',
                },
                font: {
                    main: 'Inter, sans-serif',
                    title: 'Inter, sans-serif',
                    mono: 'monospace',
                },
            }}
        >
            <main />
        </AnvilRoot>
    )
}
```

| Category | Keys | CSS variables |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spacing` | a number (px), default `4` | `--avl-spacing-x1` … `--avl-spacing-x20` |
| `font` | `main`, `title`, `mono` | `--avl-font-main` … |
| `fontSize` | `body`, `caption`, `labelSmall`, `label`, `labelLarge`, `h1`–`h6` | `--avl-font-size-label-small` … |
| `fontWeight` | `regular`, `medium`, `semibold`, `bold` | `--avl-font-weight-bold` … |
| `radius` | `small`, `medium`, `large`, `button`, `full` | `--avl-radius-medium` … |
| `shadow` | `small`, `medium`, `large` | `--avl-shadow-small` … |
| `ease` | `out`, `in`, `smooth`, `bounce` | `--avl-ease-out` … |
| `easeLength` | `short`, `normal`, `slow` | `--avl-ease-length-short` … |
| `outlineSize`, `disabledOpacity` | strings | `--avl-outline-size`, `--avl-disabled-opacity` |

---

<!-- file: docs/composition.md -->

# Composition: `render`, refs, className

AnvilUI is built on [Base UI](https://base-ui.com). Base UI patterns apply everywhere.

## `render` instead of `asChild`

There is **no `asChild`** prop. To render a part as another element or component, pass `render`:

```tsx
import {
    Button,
    Dialog,
    DialogPopup,
    DialogTitle,
    DialogTrigger,
    IconButton,
    Menu,
    MenuItem,
    MenuPopup,
    MenuTrigger,
} from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    return (
        <>
            <Dialog>
                <DialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Open</DialogTrigger>
                <DialogPopup>
                    <DialogTitle>Hi</DialogTitle>
                </DialogPopup>
            </Dialog>

            <Menu>
                <MenuTrigger
                    render={<IconButton icon="more_vert" aria-label="More" />}
                />
                <MenuPopup>
                    <MenuItem>Rename</MenuItem>
                </MenuPopup>
            </Menu>

            {/* A button that's a link: not a <button>, so nativeButton={false} */}
            <Button render={<a href="/settings" />} nativeButton={false}>
                Settings
            </Button>
        </>
    )
}
```

- `render` merges props, `className` and `ref` into the element you pass.
- All Trigger and Close parts (`DialogTrigger`, `DialogClose`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverClose`, `MenuTrigger`, `BottomSheetTrigger`, `BottomSheetClose`, `NavigationDrawerTrigger`) render a **bare, unstyled `<button>`** unless you pass `render`.
- When `render` swaps a button for a non-button element (`<a>`, `<div>`), add `nativeButton={false}`.
- Router links: `render={<Link to="/x" />}` (React Router) or `render={<Link href="/x" />}` (Next.js) on nav items, `ListItem`, `PreviewCardTrigger`, `Button` (+ `nativeButton={false}`).

## Refs and props

- Every component takes `ref` (React 19 `ref` prop) and passes unknown props to its main element.
- `className` is merged with the library's classes, never replaced. On Base UI-based parts it can also be a function of state: `className={(state) => state.open ? 'open' : ''}`.
- **Field-like components put `className` on the outer wrapper** (so width and margins work) and `ref` on the input: `Input`, `Textarea`, `DateInput`. `Select`, `Combobox`, `Search` put `className` on the field wrapper; their other props go to the Base UI Root, which renders no element.
- `Tooltip` puts `className` on the bubble. `FABMenu` puts it on the FAB.

## State props

Stateful components work controlled or uncontrolled, with Base UI's names:

| State | Props | Callback signature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| value | `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` | `(value, eventDetails) => void`. The **value**, not an event. |
| checked | `checked` / `defaultChecked` / `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean, eventDetails) => void` (Checkbox, Switch) |
| pressed | `pressed` / `defaultPressed` / `onPressedChange` | `(pressed: boolean, eventDetails) => void` (Toggle, FilterChip) |
| open | `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean, eventDetails) => void` (Dialog, Popover, Menu, Select, …) |

Because the value comes first, a `useState` setter can be passed directly: `onValueChange={setTab}`, `onCheckedChange={setEnabled}`.

There is no `onChange` on Checkbox, Switch, Select, Slider, Tabs, RadioGroup or ToggleGroup. `Input` and `Textarea` take both native `onChange` (an event) and `onValueChange` (a string).

## Base UI docs for inherited props

Each page lists AnvilUI's own props. Parts also take every prop of the Base UI part they wrap. Those are documented in the installed Base UI package: `node_modules/@base-ui/react/docs/react/components/<name>.md`.

---

<!-- file: docs/forms.md -->

# Forms

Controls are plain form elements: give them `name` and read them with `FormData`, or control them with state. `Field` adds helper text, error messages and validation to one control.

```tsx
import {
    Button,
    Checkbox,
    Field,
    FieldDescription,
    FieldError,
    Input,
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    Switch,
    Textarea,
} from 'anvilui'

const roles = { viewer: 'Viewer', editor: 'Editor', admin: 'Admin' }

export function SignupForm() {
    return (
        <form
            style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16, maxWidth: 400 }}
            onSubmit={(event) => {
                event.preventDefault()
                const data = new FormData(event.currentTarget)
                console.log(Object.fromEntries(data))
            }}
        >
            <Field name="email">
                <Input label="Email" type="email" required />
                <FieldDescription>
                    We'll send a confirmation link.
                </FieldDescription>
                <FieldError />
            </Field>

            <Field name="role">
                <Select label="Role" items={roles} defaultValue="viewer">
                    {Object.entries(roles).map(([value, label]) => (
                        <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>
                            {label}
                        </SelectItem>
                    ))}
                </Select>
            </Field>

            <Textarea label="About you" name="bio" rows={3} />

            <label style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, alignItems: 'center' }}>
                <Switch name="newsletter" defaultChecked />
                Send me the newsletter
            </label>

            <label style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, alignItems: 'center' }}>
                <Checkbox name="terms" required />I accept the terms
            </label>

            <Button type="submit">Sign up</Button>
        </form>
    )
}
```

Rules:

- **`Button` defaults to `type="button"`.** Pass `type="submit"` to submit a form.
- Text fields (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Combobox`, `DateInput`, `TimePicker`) take their own `label`. There is no `FieldLabel` or `Label` component.
- `Checkbox`, `Switch` and `Radio` have **no `label` prop**. Wrap them in a `<label>` with the text.
- Put the `name` on `Field` (or on the control when there's no Field).
- Native rules (`required`, `type="email"`, `minLength`, `pattern`, …) block a plain `<form>`'s submit and show in `FieldError`. This includes `<Checkbox required />` and `<DateInput required />`.
- Custom rules: `validate={(value) => value ? null : 'Required'}` returns an error string or `null`. A failing `validate` blocks submit once it has run, so on a plain `<form>` use `validationMode="onBlur"` or `"onChange"` with it (the default is `"onSubmit"`). Keep a final check in `onSubmit` for anything that must hold.
- Controls that work inside `Field`: `Input`, `Textarea`, `DateInput`, `Select`, `Combobox`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `RadioGroup`, `Slider`.
- `Button loading` disables the button, so it also blocks repeat submits.
- `Select` with `name` submits the item's `value`, not its label.
- Server errors: `<Field invalid>` plus `<FieldError match>` with your message (`match` true shows it whenever the field is invalid).
- Values: `DateInput` and `Calendar` use `"YYYY-MM-DD"`, `TimePicker` `"HH:mm"`, `Slider` a number (or `number[]`).
- There is no form library integration and no `Form` component. A plain `<form>` works. With react-hook-form, use controlled props (`value` + `onValueChange` / `checked` + `onCheckedChange`) in `Controller`.

See [field.md](field.md), [input.md](input.md), [select.md](select.md), [checkbox.md](checkbox.md).

---

<!-- file: docs/icons.md -->

# Icons

AnvilUI uses **Material Symbols (Rounded)**, an icon font that ships with the package. Icons are **name strings**, not components.

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, IconButton } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    return (
        <>
            <Button startIcon="add">New</Button>
            <IconButton icon="delete" aria-label="Delete" />
            <Icon
                name="favorite"
                style={{ fontSize: 32, color: 'var(--avl-color-error)' }}
            />
        </>
    )
}
```

- Names are snake_case Material Symbols names: `home`, `settings`, `arrow_back`, `more_vert`, `delete`, `edit`, `search`, `close`, `check`, `add`, `menu`, `person`, `mail`, `notifications`, `favorite`, `share`, `download`, `upload`, `visibility`, `logout`, `dark_mode`, `light_mode`. Browse: https://fonts.google.com/icons
- The prop type is `MaterialSymbol` (a union of every valid name), so a typo is a type error. To type your own data: `import type { MaterialSymbol } from 'anvilui'`, e.g. `const nav: { icon: MaterialSymbol; label: string }[] = [...]`. A plain `string` won't type-check.
- To check a name offline, search the list in `node_modules/material-symbols/index.d.ts` (the `MaterialSymbols` tuple).
- Don't import icon components from `lucide-react`, `@mui/icons-material` or `react-icons` into `startIcon` / `icon` props. Those props take strings.
- Props that take icons: `startIcon`, `endIcon` (Button, Toggle, Chip, MenuItem, …), `icon` (IconButton, FAB, Tabs tab, nav items, …), `name` (Icon).

## Icon

```ts
type IconProps = Omit<React.ComponentProps<'span'>, 'children'> & {
    name: MaterialSymbol // required
}
```

- Renders a `<span>`. Size follows `font-size`; color follows `color`.
- Decorative by default (`aria-hidden`). Give it `aria-label` to make it a labeled image.
- Takes no children: `<Icon name="home" />`, not `<Icon>home</Icon>`.

---

<!-- file: docs/morph.md -->

# morph and morphBetween

Animate one element growing into another while the view changes (Material's container transform), using View Transitions.

```ts
import { morph, morphBetween } from 'anvilui'
import type { MorphOptions } from 'anvilui'

morph(id: string, update: () => void, options?: MorphOptions): Promise<void>
morphBetween(from: HTMLElement, update: () => void, getTo: () => HTMLElement | null, options?: MorphOptions): Promise<void>
type MorphOptions = { duration?: number /* ms */; easing?: string }
```

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, Card, CardTitle, morph } from 'anvilui'

const albums = [
    { id: 'a1', title: 'Blue' },
    { id: 'a2', title: 'Red' },
]

export function Albums() {
    const [open, setOpen] = useState<string | null>(null)

    if (open) {
        return (
            <Card data-morph-id={open} style={{ minHeight: 300 }}>
                <Button onClick={() => morph(open, () => setOpen(null))}>
                    Back
                </Button>
            </Card>
        )
    }
    return albums.map((a) => (
        <Card
            key={a.id}
            clickable
            data-morph-id={a.id}
            onClick={() => morph(a.id, () => setOpen(a.id))}
        >
            <CardTitle>{a.title}</CardTitle>
        </Card>
    ))
}
```

- Give both elements the same `data-morph-id`.
- `update` must change the view **synchronously** (set state, or `navigate(to, { flushSync: true })` in React Router).
- Without View Transitions support, or with reduced motion, `update` just runs.
- `Dialog` and `Popover` take `morph` (boolean) to do this between their trigger and popup.

---

<!-- file: docs/button.md -->

# Button

A button with a text label and optional icons. Renders a `<button type="button">`.

```ts
import { Button } from 'anvilui'
import type { ButtonProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fillType` | `'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'text'` | `'filled'` | The style (other libraries call this `variant`). |
| `color` | `ComponentColor` | `'primary'` | `primary`, `tonal`, `success`, `warning`, `error`, `container`, `surface`. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'normal' \| 'big'` | `'normal'` | 32, 40 or 48px tall. |
| `startIcon` | `MaterialSymbol` | | Icon name before the label, e.g. `'add'`. |
| `endIcon` | `MaterialSymbol` | | Icon name after the label. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Spinner in place of `startIcon`; ignores clicks; keeps focus. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `type` | `'button' \| 'submit' \| 'reset'` | `'button'` | Pass `'submit'` in forms. |
| `render` | `ReactElement` | | Render as another element, e.g. `<a href>` (+ `nativeButton={false}`). |

Also takes Base UI Button props (`focusableWhenDisabled`, `nativeButton`) and all `<button>` attributes. Base UI docs: `node_modules/@base-ui/react/docs/react/components/button.md`.

## Example

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false)
    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8 }}>
            <Button startIcon="add">New</Button>
            <Button fillType="outlined" color="container">
                Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button fillType="text">Learn more</Button>
            <Button color="error" startIcon="delete">
                Delete
            </Button>
            <Button loading={saving} onClick={() => setSaving(true)}>
                {saving ? 'Saving' : 'Save'}
            </Button>
            <Button
                render={<a href="/docs" />}
                nativeButton={false}
                endIcon="arrow_forward"
            >
                Docs
            </Button>
        </div>
    )
}
```

## Notes

- Mapping from other libraries: `variant="outline"` → `fillType="outlined"`, `variant="ghost" | "link"` → `fillType="text"`, `variant="secondary"` → `color="container"` or `color="tonal"`, `variant="destructive"` → `color="error"`.
- Icon-only? Use [IconButton](icon-button.md). Grouped buttons: [SplitButton](split-button.md). Hold-to-confirm: [HoldButton](hold-button.md). On/off: [Toggle](toggle.md).
- No `fullWidth` prop: use `style={{ width: '100%' }}`.

---

<!-- file: docs/icon-button.md -->

# IconButton

A round 40px button with only an icon. `aria-label` is required.

```ts
import { IconButton } from 'anvilui'
import type { IconButtonProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `MaterialSymbol` | required | Icon name, e.g. `'delete'`. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | required | What the button does. |
| `fillType` | `'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'text'` | `'filled'` | |
| `color` | `ComponentColor` | `'primary'` | |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |

Takes no `children` and has **no `size` prop** (always 40px). Also takes Base UI Button props and `<button>` attributes.

## Example

```tsx
import { IconButton, Tooltip } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    return (
        <>
            <IconButton icon="add" aria-label="Add" />
            {/* The usual "toolbar" look: no fill, neutral color */}
            <IconButton
                icon="more_vert"
                aria-label="More options"
                fillType="text"
                color="container"
            />
            <Tooltip label="Delete">
                <IconButton
                    icon="delete"
                    aria-label="Delete"
                    fillType="outlined"
                    color="error"
                />
            </Tooltip>
        </>
    )
}
```

## Notes

- Default is a filled primary circle. For plain icon buttons in bars and lists, use `fillType="text" color="container"`.
- On/off icon buttons (favorite, bold): `<Toggle icon="favorite" aria-label="Favorite" />` ([toggle.md](toggle.md)).

---

<!-- file: docs/split-button.md -->

# SplitButton

Joins `Button`s and `IconButton`s into one segmented group. Renders a `<div role="group">`.

```ts
import { SplitButton } from 'anvilui'
import type { SplitButtonProps } from 'anvilui' // = React.ComponentProps<'div'>
```

No props of its own. Style each button inside yourself; give them all the same `color`, `fillType` and `size`.

```tsx
import {
    Button,
    IconButton,
    Menu,
    MenuItem,
    MenuPopup,
    MenuTrigger,
    SplitButton,
} from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    return (
        <SplitButton aria-label="Save">
            <Button startIcon="save">Save</Button>
            <Menu>
                <MenuTrigger
                    render={
                        <IconButton
                            icon="arrow_drop_down"
                            aria-label="More save options"
                        />
                    }
                />
                <MenuPopup align="end">
                    <MenuItem>Save as copy</MenuItem>
                    <MenuItem>Save as template</MenuItem>
                </MenuPopup>
            </Menu>
        </SplitButton>
    )
}
```

---

<!-- file: docs/hold-button.md -->

# HoldButton

A button for destructive actions: press and hold until it fills, instead of a confirm dialog. Releasing early cancels.

```ts
import { HoldButton } from 'anvilui'
import type { HoldButtonProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## Props

All `Button` props except `loading`, plus:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onConfirm` | `() => void` | required | Called after holding for `holdDuration`. |
| `holdDuration` | `number` (ms) | `1500` | |

```tsx
import { HoldButton } from 'anvilui'

export function Example({ onDelete }: { onDelete: () => void }) {
    return (
        <HoldButton color="error" startIcon="delete" onConfirm={onDelete}>
            Hold to delete
        </HoldButton>
    )
}
```

- Use `onConfirm`, not `onClick` (`onClick` also fires on a short press).
- Works with Space/Enter held. Screen reader clicks, which can't hold, confirm immediately.

---

<!-- file: docs/toggle.md -->

# Toggle

A button that stays on or off (Bold, Favorite). Sets `aria-pressed`. Off it's neutral; on it fills with `color`.

```ts
import { Toggle } from 'anvilui'
import type { ToggleProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pressed` / `defaultPressed` | `boolean` | `false` | On state. |
| `onPressedChange` | `(pressed: boolean, details) => void` | | |
| `color` | `ComponentColor` | `'primary'` | Color while on. |
| `fillType` | `'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'text'` | `'filled'` | Look while off. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | Label (text toggle). |
| `startIcon`, `endIcon` | `MaterialSymbol` | | Text toggle only. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'normal' \| 'big'` | `'normal'` | Text toggle only. |
| `icon` | `MaterialSymbol` | | Makes it a round icon toggle. Requires `aria-label`; no children or size. |
| `value` | `string` | | Identifies it in a Base UI ToggleGroup. |

Either `children` or `icon` + `aria-label`, not both.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Toggle } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    const [favorite, setFavorite] = useState(false)
    return (
        <>
            <Toggle startIcon="format_bold" defaultPressed>
                Bold
            </Toggle>
            <Toggle
                icon="favorite"
                aria-label="Favorite"
                color="error"
                pressed={favorite}
                onPressedChange={setFavorite}
            />
        </>
    )
}
```

For a row of exclusive options use [ToggleGroup](toggle-group.md). For filter chips use `FilterChip` ([chip.md](chip.md)).

---

<!-- file: docs/toggle-group.md -->

# ToggleGroup

A segmented control: a row of options with a sliding selection pill. One selected by default; `multiple` for several.

```ts
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from 'anvilui'
import type { ToggleGroupProps, ToggleGroupItemProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## ToggleGroup props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | single: `Value`; multiple: `string[]` | | **Single mode takes one value, not an array.** |
| `onValueChange` | single: `(value: Value, details) => void`; multiple: `(value: string[], details) => void` | | |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Allow several on at once. |
| `color` | `ComponentColor` | `'primary'` | |
| `fillType` | `'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'text'` | `'filled'` | |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'normal' \| 'big'` | `'normal'` | |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | | |
| `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` | `string` | | Name the group (both are passed through). |

Single mode is a Base UI RadioGroup; multiple mode is a Base UI ToggleGroup. `Value` is inferred from `value`, so a union-typed `useState<'list' | 'grid'>` setter can be passed straight to `onValueChange`.

## ToggleGroupItem props

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `Value` (string in `multiple`) | Required. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Label. |
| `startIcon`, `endIcon` | `MaterialSymbol` | |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | |

## Example

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    const [view, setView] = useState('list')
    const [days, setDays] = useState<string[]>(['mon'])
    return (
        <>
            <ToggleGroup aria-label="View" value={view} onValueChange={setView}>
                <ToggleGroupItem value="list" startIcon="list">
                    List
                </ToggleGroupItem>
                <ToggleGroupItem value="grid" startIcon="grid_view">
                    Grid
                </ToggleGroupItem>
            </ToggleGroup>

            <ToggleGroup
                multiple
                aria-label="Days"
                value={days}
                onValueChange={setDays}
                fillType="outlined"
            >
                <ToggleGroupItem value="mon">Mon</ToggleGroupItem>
                <ToggleGroupItem value="tue">Tue</ToggleGroupItem>
                <ToggleGroupItem value="wed">Wed</ToggleGroupItem>
            </ToggleGroup>
        </>
    )
}
```

Use it for 2–5 short options. For longer lists use [RadioGroup](radio-group.md) or [Select](select.md).

---

<!-- file: docs/fab.md -->

# FAB

The floating action button: the screen's main action. You position it (usually `position: fixed`, bottom-end).

```ts
import { FAB } from 'anvilui'
import type { FABProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `MaterialSymbol` | required | |
| `label` | `string` | | Visible text: makes it an extended FAB. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | required without `label` | |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'normal' \| 'big'` | `'normal'` | 40, 56 or 96px. |
| `color` | `ComponentColor` | `'primary'` | |
| `fillType` | `'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'text'` | `'filled'` | |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `true` | Drifts toward a nearby mouse cursor. |

Takes no children. Also Base UI Button props.

```tsx
import { FAB } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    return (
        <>
            <FAB
                icon="edit"
                aria-label="Compose"
                style={{ position: 'fixed', insetInlineEnd: 16, bottom: 16 }}
            />
            <FAB icon="add" label="New task" color="tonal" />
        </>
    )
}
```

`sticky` only adds a small `translate` toward the cursor, so it works with any `position` you set.

For a FAB that opens several actions, use [FABMenu](fab-menu.md).

---

<!-- file: docs/fab-menu.md -->

# FABMenu

A FAB that opens a stack of labeled actions. You position it.

```ts
import { FABMenu, FABMenuItem } from 'anvilui'
import type { FABMenuProps, FABMenuItemProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## FABMenu props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `MaterialSymbol` | required | Icon while closed. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | required | |
| `children` | `FABMenuItem`s | required | |
| `closeIcon` | `MaterialSymbol` | `'close'` | Icon while open. |
| `color` | `ComponentColor` | `'primary'` | Items use the role's container shade. |
| `fillType` | `'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'text'` | `'filled'` | |
| `side` | `'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'inline-start' \| 'inline-end'` | `'top'` | |
| `align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'end'` | |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `true` | |
| `className` | `string` | | Goes on the FAB. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` | | | Base UI Menu.Root state. |

## FABMenuItem props

`icon: MaterialSymbol` (required), `children` (label, required), `color?: ComponentColor`, `onClick`, `disabled`, plus Base UI Menu.Item props.

```tsx
import { FABMenu, FABMenuItem } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    return (
        <div style={{ position: 'fixed', insetInlineEnd: 16, bottom: 16 }}>
            <FABMenu icon="add" aria-label="Create">
                <FABMenuItem
                    icon="description"
                    onClick={() => console.log('doc')}
                >
                    Document
                </FABMenuItem>
                <FABMenuItem
                    icon="folder"
                    onClick={() => console.log('folder')}
                >
                    Folder
                </FABMenuItem>
            </FABMenu>
        </div>
    )
}
```

Needs `AnvilRoot` (the items portal into it).

<!-- file: docs/chip.md -->

# Chip, FilterChip, InputChip

Compact elements for actions, filters and entered values.

```ts
import { Chip, FilterChip, InputChip } from 'anvilui'
import type { ChipProps, FilterChipProps, InputChipProps } from 'anvilui'
```

| Component | Is | Own props |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Chip` | a button (suggestion / quick action) | `startIcon?: MaterialSymbol`; Base UI Button props |
| `FilterChip` | an on/off toggle with a checkmark | `pressed` / `defaultPressed` / `onPressedChange(pressed, details)`; Base UI Toggle props |
| `InputChip` | a removable value (`<span>`) | `onRemove: () => void` (required), `removeLabel?: string` (default `'Remove'`), `startIcon?`, `disabled?` |

Chips have no `color`, `fillType` or `size` props.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Chip, FilterChip, InputChip } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    const [vegan, setVegan] = useState(false)
    const [tags, setTags] = useState(['react', 'design'])
    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
            <Chip startIcon="event" onClick={() => console.log('added')}>
                Add to calendar
            </Chip>
            <FilterChip pressed={vegan} onPressedChange={setVegan}>
                Vegan
            </FilterChip>
            {tags.map((tag) => (
                <InputChip
                    key={tag}
                    removeLabel={`Remove ${tag}`}
                    onRemove={() => setTags(tags.filter((t) => t !== tag))}
                >
                    {tag}
                </InputChip>
            ))}
        </div>
    )
}
```

- `InputChip` animates out, then calls `onRemove`. Remove the item from your state there; if you keep it, the chip reappears.
- Lay chips out in a flex row with `gap`.

---

<!-- file: docs/input.md -->

# Input

A text field with a floating label inside its border.

```ts
import { Input } from 'anvilui'
import type { InputProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | | Floating label. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'normal'` | `'normal'` | Small's label acts as a placeholder. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string` | | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string, details) => void` | | The string. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` | | The native event also works. |
| `className` | `string` | | On the **wrapper** `<label>` (width, margins). |
| `ref` | | | On the `<input>`. |
| everything else | `<input>` attributes | | `type`, `name`, `placeholder`, `required`, `disabled`, `autoComplete`, … go on the `<input>`. |

No `startIcon` / `endIcon` / `error` / `helperText` props. For helper and error text wrap it in a [Field](field.md). For a search bar use [Search](search.md).

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Field, FieldError, Input } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16, width: 320 }}>
            <Input label="Name" name="name" defaultValue="Ada" />
            <Field validationMode="onBlur">
                <Input
                    label="Email"
                    type="email"
                    required
                    value={email}
                    onValueChange={setEmail}
                />
                <FieldError />
            </Field>
            <Input size="small" label="Filter" />
        </div>
    )
}
```

The field is `width: 100%`-friendly: give the wrapper a width with `className` or put it in a grid.

---

<!-- file: docs/textarea.md -->

# Textarea

A multi-line text field. Same API as [Input](input.md), with `<textarea>` attributes (`rows`, …).

```ts
import { Textarea } from 'anvilui'
import type { TextareaProps } from 'anvilui'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | | Floating label. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'normal'` | `'normal'` | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string, details) => void` | | Or native `onChange`. |
| `className` | `string` | | On the wrapper. |

```tsx
import { Textarea } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    return <Textarea label="Message" name="message" rows={4} />
}
```

<!-- file: docs/field.md -->

# Field, FieldDescription, FieldError

Wraps one control to add helper text, an error message and validation. The control keeps its own `label`. **There is no `FieldLabel`.**

```ts
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError } from 'anvilui'
import type {
    FieldProps,
    FieldDescriptionProps,
    FieldErrorProps,
} from 'anvilui'
```

## Field props (Base UI Field.Root)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | | Form field name (overrides the control's). |
| `validate` | `(value, formValues) => string \| string[] \| null \| Promise<…>` | | Return an error message, or `null` when valid. |
| `validationMode` | `'onSubmit' \| 'onBlur' \| 'onChange'` | `'onSubmit'` | When to validate. Outside a `<form>`, use `onBlur` or `onChange`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | | Force the invalid state (e.g. a server error). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | | Disables the control. |

## FieldError props

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | `boolean \| keyof ValidityState` | Show only for one problem (`'valueMissing'`, `'typeMismatch'`, …), or `true` to show whenever invalid. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Message. Without it, shows the browser's or `validate`'s message. |

`FieldDescription` is helper text; hidden while an error shows.

```tsx
import { Button, Field, FieldDescription, FieldError, Input } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    return (
        <form
            onSubmit={(e) => e.preventDefault()}
            style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16, width: 320 }}
        >
            <Field
                name="username"
                validate={(value) =>
                    String(value).length < 3 ? 'At least 3 characters' : null
                }
            >
                <Input label="Username" required />
                <FieldDescription>Shown on your profile.</FieldDescription>
                <FieldError match="valueMissing">Choose a username.</FieldError>
                <FieldError match="customError" />
            </Field>
            <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
        </form>
    )
}
```

Works with `Input`, `Textarea`, `DateInput`, `Select`, `Combobox`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `RadioGroup`, `Slider`. A required checkbox: `<Field name="terms"><label><Checkbox required /> I accept</label><FieldError match="valueMissing">Please accept the terms.</FieldError></Field>`. On a plain `<form>`, a custom `validate` only blocks submit after it has run: use `validationMode="onBlur"` or `"onChange"` (see [forms.md](forms.md)). Base UI docs: `node_modules/@base-ui/react/docs/react/components/field.md`.

---

<!-- file: docs/select.md -->

# Select, SelectItem

A dropdown to pick one option (or several with `multiple`). Looks like `Input`.

```ts
import { Select, SelectItem } from 'anvilui'
import type { SelectProps, SelectItemProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## Select props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `SelectItem`s | | |
| `items` | `Record<string, ReactNode>` or `{ value, label }[]` | | **Pass it** so the field shows the label, not the raw value. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Value \| null` (array with `multiple`) | | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: Value \| null, details) => void` | | The value, not an event. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | | Floating label. |
| `placeholder` | `ReactNode` | | Shown when nothing is selected. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'normal'` | `'normal'` | |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly` | | | |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` | | | |
| `itemToStringLabel` | `(value) => string` | | For object values. |
| `className` | `string` | | On the field wrapper. |

Other props go to Base UI `Select.Root`, which renders no element: `id`, `style` and `ref` are not applied. Base UI docs: `node_modules/@base-ui/react/docs/react/components/select.md`.

## SelectItem props

`value` (required), `children` (the label), `disabled`.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Select, SelectItem } from 'anvilui'

const countries = [
    { value: 'us', label: 'United States' },
    { value: 'fr', label: 'France' },
    { value: 'jp', label: 'Japan' },
]

export function Example() {
    const [country, setCountry] = useState<string | null>('fr')
    return (
        <Select
            label="Country"
            items={countries}
            value={country}
            onValueChange={setCountry}
            className="country-field"
        >
            {countries.map((c) => (
                <SelectItem key={c.value} value={c.value}>
                    {c.label}
                </SelectItem>
            ))}
        </Select>
    )
}
```

- No `SelectTrigger`, `SelectContent` or `SelectValue` parts: `Select` renders the field and the popup. Only items go inside.
- For a searchable list use [Combobox](combobox.md).

---

<!-- file: docs/combobox.md -->

# Combobox, ComboboxItem

A text field that filters a list as you type and picks one item. **Children are a render function**, and `items` is the list to filter.

```ts
import { Combobox, ComboboxItem } from 'anvilui'
import type { ComboboxProps, ComboboxItemProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## Combobox props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly Item[]` | | The options. |
| `children` | `(item: Item, index: number) => ReactNode` | required | Renders one `ComboboxItem`. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Item \| null` | | The picked item. |
| `onValueChange` | `(item: Item \| null, details) => void` | | |
| `inputValue` / `onInputValueChange` | `string` / `(text, details) => void` | | The typed text. |
| `itemToStringLabel` | `(item) => string` | | Required for object items. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | | Floating label. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | | |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` | | Shown when nothing matches; without it the popup hides. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'normal'` | `'normal'` | |
| `className` | `string` | | On the field wrapper. |
| `name`, `disabled`, `required`, `filter`, `limit` | | | Base UI Combobox.Root props. |

## ComboboxItem props

`value: Item` (required), `children` (label), `disabled`.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Combobox, ComboboxItem } from 'anvilui'

type User = { id: number; name: string }
const users: User[] = [
    { id: 1, name: 'Ada Lovelace' },
    { id: 2, name: 'Alan Turing' },
]
const fruits = ['Apple', 'Banana', 'Cherry']

export function Example() {
    const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(null)
    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16, width: 320 }}>
            <Combobox label="Fruit" items={fruits} empty="No fruit found">
                {(fruit: string) => (
                    <ComboboxItem key={fruit} value={fruit}>
                        {fruit}
                    </ComboboxItem>
                )}
            </Combobox>

            <Combobox
                label="Assignee"
                items={users}
                value={user}
                onValueChange={setUser}
                itemToStringLabel={(u: User) => u.name}
            >
                {(u: User) => (
                    <ComboboxItem key={u.id} value={u}>
                        {u.name}
                    </ComboboxItem>
                )}
            </Combobox>
        </div>
    )
}
```

Base UI docs: `node_modules/@base-ui/react/docs/react/components/combobox.md`.

<!-- file: docs/search.md -->

# Search, SearchItem

A Material 3 search bar with a suggestion list. `aria-label` is required. **Children are a render function** over `items`. The value is the typed text.

```ts
import { Search, SearchItem } from 'anvilui'
import type { SearchProps, SearchItemProps } from 'anvilui'
```

## Search props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` | `string` | required | |
| `children` | `(item: Item, index: number) => ReactNode` | required | Renders one `SearchItem`. |
| `items` | `readonly Item[]` | | Suggestions, filtered as you type. Pass `[]` for none. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string` | | The typed text. |
| `onValueChange` | `(text: string, details) => void` | | |
| `placeholder` | `string` | | |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` | | Shown when nothing matches. |
| `clearLabel` | `string` | `'Clear'` | Name of the clear button. |
| `className` | `string` | | On the bar. |
| `itemToStringValue`, `filter`, `limit`, `openOnInputClick` | | | Base UI Autocomplete.Root props. |

## SearchItem props

`value: Item` (required), `startIcon?: MaterialSymbol`, `children`.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Search, SearchItem } from 'anvilui'

const recent = ['invoices', 'travel', 'receipts']

export function Example() {
    const [query, setQuery] = useState('')
    return (
        <Search
            aria-label="Search mail"
            placeholder="Search mail"
            items={recent}
            value={query}
            onValueChange={setQuery}
        >
            {(item: string) => (
                <SearchItem key={item} value={item} startIcon="history">
                    {item}
                </SearchItem>
            )}
        </Search>
    )
}
```

To filter a page's own content with no suggestion list, pass `items={[]}` and a render function that returns `null`, then filter your data with the typed text:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { List, ListItem, Search } from 'anvilui'

const people = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Alan Turing', 'Grace Hopper']

export function FilterExample() {
    const [query, setQuery] = useState('')
    const shown = people.filter((p) => p.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()))
    return (
        <>
            <Search aria-label="Filter people" placeholder="Filter people" items={[]} value={query} onValueChange={setQuery}>
                {() => null}
            </Search>
            <List>
                {shown.map((p) => <ListItem key={p} label={p} />)}
            </List>
        </>
    )
}
```

<!-- file: docs/checkbox.md -->

# Checkbox

A checkbox. **No `label` prop**: wrap it in a `<label>`.

```ts
import { Checkbox } from 'anvilui'
import type { CheckboxProps } from 'anvilui' // = Base UI Checkbox.Root props
```

## Props (Base UI Checkbox.Root)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` / `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean, details) => void` | | Not `onChange`. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a dash. |
| `name`, `value` | `string` | | For forms. |
| `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | |

Base UI docs: `node_modules/@base-ui/react/docs/react/components/checkbox.md`.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Checkbox } from 'anvilui'

export function Example() {
    const [agreed, setAgreed] = useState(false)
    return (
        <label style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, alignItems: 'center' }}>
            <Checkbox checked={agreed} onCheckedChange={setAgreed} />I agree to
            the terms
        </label>
    )
}
```

In a list row, put it in `ListItem`'s `start` with `render={<label />}` so the whole row toggles it ([list.md](list.md)).
